content.text: {"policies":[],"notes":"Abstaining. The evidence is too large and noisy to find a clause that preserves every query's recall in all seven conditions. Stops would mainly help votes743/votes527/votes310 (guarded parent costs ~35-100ms there), but at cp16/32/64 those filters mostly have qualifying_count<10 (a stop is impossible) or recall below the parent's. Where qualifying_count>=10, the forced-stop hits are frequently below parent (for example 7/10 on votes527, 8-9/10 on votes310 vs a 10/10 parent), and tenth_distance, frontier_gap and top10_new_since_previous do not separate safe cases from unsafe ones reliably. For the cheap filters (unfiltered, votes192/108/32), stop times at cp16-64 are only ~1.5-3.5ms against parent/noop times of ~5-20ms, but the stops frequently lose hits relative to the parent: unfiltered cp16 with frontier_gap>=0.1 still shows 8/10 or 9/10 in several cases, and the cases that are safe overlap in feature space with the lossy ones. Because the condition is zero per-query recall loss in all seven conditions plus a >=.95 per-condition floor, any rule I wrote from rounded features would risk violating the guarantee. Abstaining is the conservative choice."}
